question: Decision 90/655/EEC1 amends Decision 87/277/EEC23. The Council thereby ‘adapted’ the reference period used to calculate the German Democratic Republic’s quota and established a method4 for amending this allocation5 in the event of a change to the number of Member States67with a view to applying it in the future8. Proportional adjustments were ruled out as they risked jeopardising relative stability9.

Since 2021, the Commission’s proposals to the Council have entailed combining the quotas of the EU and the United Kingdom before reallocating them in line with Decision 90/655/EEC, including the United Kingdom, and then applying the ‘Brexit effect’ by means of a proportional adjustment10. As a result, in 202111, only Spain’s and Portugal’s quotas were reduced, while those of other Member States increased12.

The other Member States did not reach the standard amount of one hundred tonnes allocated by Decisions 90/655/EEC and 87/277/EEC in 202313 and 202414. Since 2021, there have been changes to the relative positions of Member States, which has an effect beyond the total allowable catches (TACs). 1.
Why has the Commission not applied the method accepted by the Council in 1990, which maintains relative stability?
Why has the Commission not proposed to the Council a regulation that avoids legal effects beyond what is established in connection with the TACs?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) As set out in our answer to E-002042/2023, the annual EU quotas for cod in Svalbard waters and international waters of the International Council of the Exploration of the Sea (ICES) subarea 1 and division 2b continue to be allocated to the Member States concerned in accordance with Council Decision 87/277/EEC1, as amended by Council Decision 90/655/EEC2.

The Commission considers that the 1990 Decision did not address future allocations between Member States in the event of future accessions to the EU and did not pertain to the accession of a new Member State. In 2003, the Council allocated a fixed share of that EU quota to Poland in accordance with the share set out in Annex XII to the Act of Accession of Poland to the EU3.

In that case, the approach followed by the Council was to continue to apply the legal basis for the allocation to existing Member States, while also taking into account the allocation to new Member States. That approach has also been applied since the withdrawal of the United Kingdom (UK) from the EU.

The existing legal framework regarding allocations continues to be applied, while also taking into account the necessary adjustments following the UK’s withdrawal from the EU. In that case, the EU quota is subject to adaptations as set out in Annex 36(E) to the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA)4, and the Member States quotas thereunder are adjusted accordingly.

Finally, as set out in our answer to E-002042/2023, as the current legal framework5 provides for an objective and fair allocation of quotas, the Commission does not intend to propose to reopen Council Decision 87/277/EEC.
1 87/277/EEC: Council Decision of 18 May 1987 on the allocation of the catch possibilities for cod in the

Spitsbergen and Bear Island area and in Division 3M as defined in the NAFO Convention (OJ L 135, 23.5.1987, p. 29). 2 90/655/EEC: Council Decision of 4 December 1990 amending Decision 87/277/EEC on the allocation of the catch possibilities for cod in the Spitzbergen.

3 Treaty between Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Spain, France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Finland, Sweden, United Kingdom and Czechia, Estonia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Malta, Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia, concerning the accession of Czechia, Estonia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Malta, Poland, Slovenia and Slovakia to the EU (OJ L 236, 23.9.2003, p. 17).

4 Trade and Cooperation Agreement between the EU and the European Atomic Energy Community, of the one part, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, of the other part (OJ L 149, 30.4.2021, p. 10). 5 Council Decision 87/277/EEC, Annex XII to the Act of Accession of Poland to the EU and Annex 36(E) to the TCA.
